Hi Sarah — thanks for the logs. I'll take point on reproducing this. A few quick asks to speed triage:

1) Full request body (JSON payload) for one of the failing batched calls (not just HAR) — we need the exact array shape and any extra meta fields.
2) Response headers from the 500 (especially x-request-id, x-server-node, and x-redwood-kv-status).
3) Can you confirm the SDK version you used? If it's our JS SDK, what's the version string?

Immediate suggestions to try while I repro locally:
- Increase client timeout to 60s (some backend retries can add latency)
- Try sending batches of 1 or 2 to confirm if batching correlates to failure rate
- If possible, set the routing param to model=reranker-v1-explicit to avoid automatic fallback behavior

I'll spin up a local run that mimics an 8-item batch with your payload shape and post back results plus a minimal repro. If we see consistent 5xx that reproduces, we'll push a targeted fix.

—Dylan

Subject: Re: FinLytics - Redwood integration next steps / 5xx on embeddings+reranker (patch + guidance)

Hi Sarah — quick update from infra: Dylan was able to reproduce locally when batching>4 and traced the 500 to a race in the KV cache warmup path for reranker-v1 under simultaneous batch requests. We have a short-term mitigation and a patch coming: 

Immediate mitigation (apply in staging):
- Upgrade Redwood SDK to v1.3.2 (contains a batching workaround)
- Client config: set "use_kv_cache": false for reranker-v1 until patch is rolled (example below)

Example config snippet:
const client = new Redwood.Client({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY,
  timeoutMs: 60000,
  batching: 'single_request',
  modelOverrides: { 'reranker-v1': { use_kv_cache: false } }
});

We will push a backend patch to fix the KV warmup race by EOD tomorrow and follow up once INF-7891 is updated. Patch diff attached (patch-reranker-fix.diff) and I've updated the ticket with the reproduction steps and logs.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-min windows tomorrow morning to validate staging after the patch.

—Neha Kapoor
Staff Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
